title: Battery management and DC protection for a storage plant
description:
Work package: battery management system (BMS) and DC string protection for a grid-connected lithium iron phosphate storage plant in Germany. The system team has closed the plant design and hands it over; the plant itself cannot change. Your team designs the rack BMS (one per string, identical for every rack) and writes down the requirements it derives.

Stakeholder needs:
  SN-1: usable energy 3.300 MWh at the connection point (requirement including the project margin) at end of service life, 1 h duration, within the cell manufacturer's recommended SOC window.
  SN-2: prequalification for frequency containment reserve (FCR) in Germany with 2.4 MW, symmetric.
  SN-3: DC bus of a PCS ready within 8 s of a start command.
  SN-4: safety of cells, equipment and people at all times, including faults, installation and maintenance; cells within the cell manufacturer's safety limits.
  SN-5: lowest BMS and protection cost for the plant.
  SN-6: compliance with the network operator's connection letter and technical connection rules.

Handover from the system team (end of life where it matters):
  23 strings (one per rack) of 368 cells in series: 23 modules of 16 cells, 4 temperature sensors per module.
  String current at rated power 133.5 A; string voltage at full charge 1343.2 V.
  Cell capacity at end of life 251.1 Ah. SOC window 5-95%.
  Usable energy at the connection point at end of life over the full window, net of auxiliaries: 5.632 MWh; auxiliary energy during a full 1 h discharge: 0.0684 MWh.
  PCS: 3 x PCS-2 (1704 kVA), strings on one PCS share its DC bus; DC-link capacitance 8.7 mF per PCS.
  String fuse FU-5: gBat, 400 A. Pre-arcing time by multiple of rated current: 1.6 x: 3160.0, 2 x: 325.0, 3 x: 31.6, 4 x: 5.45, 5 x: 1.4, 7 x: 0.252, 10 x: 0.0491, 15 x: 0.00777, 20 x: 0.00244 s.
  DC cable route rack to PCS 40 m per string (two conductors).
  The PCS units are transformerless; their AC outputs share one low-voltage winding of the step-up transformer, whose star point is not earthed. Earth capacitance (Y-capacitors and stray): 1.63 uF per rack, 45 uF per PCS, 0.18 nF per metre per DC conductor.
  Auxiliary supply: from the plant's medium-voltage busbar through an auxiliary transformer; each rack's 24 V control supply (MCU, contactor coil, current sensor and anything else in the rack) comes from a power supply that works down to 50% of nominal input voltage and holds up 20 ms after that.
  Rack controller interfaces: 2 CAN buses (PCS, energy management), 12 analogue channels (current, voltages on both sides of the contactor, insulation monitoring, spares).

Cell datasheet (LFP prismatic, 280 Ah, 3.2 V nominal, charge to 3.65 V, continuous 0.5 C):
  Open-circuit voltage by SOC %: 0: 2.95, 5: 3.171, 10: 3.21, 20: 3.249, 30: 3.276, 40: 3.287, 50: 3.289, 60: 3.294, 70: 3.314, 80: 3.329, 85: 3.331, 90: 3.332, 95: 3.343, 100: 3.401 V.
  Safety limit: above 3.75 V the cell must be disconnected within 100 ms.
  Short-time current limit by multiple of 1 C: 2 C: 60.5, 3 C: 11.9, 5 C: 2.39, 10 C: 0.249, 20 C: 0.0161, 50 C: 0.00184 s.
  Cell-to-cell spread in self-discharge, % of capacity per month, by cell temperature: 25 C: 0.45, 35 C: 0.9, 45 C: 1.8.

Network operator's connection letter (extract): the plant must stay connected through the following fault sequence, a fault on a neighbouring feeder with an unsuccessful automatic reclose. At t = 0 the voltage at the connection point falls to 0% for 250 ms; the faulted feeder's breaker then opens and the voltage recovers linearly from 0% towards 90% over 2 s. The breaker recloses 0.5 s after opening, onto the fault, which is still present: the voltage falls to 0% again for 250 ms and recovers the same way, and the breaker then opens for good.

Operations:
  The plant runs FCR; the operator schedules a charge to the top of the window every 14 days for SOC recalibration.
  Recalibration: the plant rests 30 min at 95% SOC and the BMS resets SOC from the open-circuit voltage.
  Between recalibrations the BMS counts charge. Current sensors are auto-zeroed while the contactor is open.
  The HVAC holds the cells at 35 C. Balancing can run 8 h per day.

Firmware team (fixed):
  Cell over-voltage is confirmed after 4 consecutive scans of the whole daisy chain, then the MCU opens the string contactor in its next control cycle.
  Overcurrent trip at 154 A from the current sensor (no daisy chain in this path); above the contactor's breaking capability the BMS keeps it closed and leaves interruption to the fuse.
  Precharge: the main contactor closes when the DC bus is within 2% of the string voltage. The BMS checks the bus voltage 1.5 s after starting precharge and aborts if it has not risen. The precharge relay is rated 30 A peak. The start sequence before precharge takes 0.5 s.

Derived requirements to write down, each traced to the stakeholder need it comes from, with a value that follows from the data: R-SOC (maximum SOC error, %), R-TRIP (maximum over-voltage disconnect time, ms), R-PRE (maximum precharge time, s), R-BAL (minimum balancing current, mA), R-BRK (minimum DC breaking current of the string contactor, A), R-RIDE (minimum time the rack's 24 V must be bridged by its hold-up, s), R-IMD (minimum system leakage capacitance rating of the insulation monitoring, uF).

Objective: minimize the BMS and protection price for the plant (monitoring chips, balancing stages, current sensor, MCU, contactor, precharge resistor and hold-up for every rack, and the insulation monitoring). The design must meet every stakeholder need, and every requirement that follows from them and from the data, whether or not it is listed here; its price must be within 5% of the cheapest design that does.
